typical_mindset: When asked for squares of every size within a grid, only the smallest (1x1) squares get counted — the idea that a 2x2 or 3x3 block of the grid is itself a square hasn't been considered as something to count separately.
explanation_strategy: Ask the child to trace a bigger square (like a 2x2 block) with a finger first, confirming it's a real square too, before recounting everything by size, one size at a time.

example_dialogue.text: Can you trace a square that's made of 4 little boxes, 2 across and 2 down?
That's a square too, even though it's bigger! Let's count all the squares of that size first, then move to the next size.

typical_mindset: Squares of the same size that overlap (share some of their little boxes) are counted as if only non-overlapping squares could exist — the child either counts an overlapping square twice by accident, or skips it entirely, because 'two squares sharing space' doesn't fit an initial mental picture of neatly separate squares.
explanation_strategy: Have the child systematically slide a same-size square window one position at a time across the grid, marking each new position found, rather than eyeballing the whole grid at once — so overlapping squares are found in an orderly sweep instead of ad hoc.

example_dialogue.text: Let's start this square in the top-left corner. Now slide it one box to the right — is that a new square too, even though it overlaps the first one?
Right — let's keep sliding one box at a time and count every position, even the overlapping ones.

typical_mindset: Every square strictly smaller than the full grid gets counted, but the grid's own outer boundary — the biggest square of all, made of every little box together — doesn't get counted as 'a square' in its own right, since it's the frame the counting happens inside rather than a shape being counted.
explanation_strategy: Ask the child whether the outer boundary of the whole grid is itself a square shape, tracing it with a finger, before finalizing the total — so the biggest size gets checked explicitly rather than assumed away.

example_dialogue.text: Trace the very outside edge of the whole grid with your finger. Is that outline itself a square?
Right, so that counts too. Did you include it in your total?
